calibration_note: HXC-159 F-17 remediation (2026-09-23): REAL-CORPUS recalibration. Prior calibration mixed corpus-1 (8 constitution/skills/*/SKILL.md, actually loaded together by BOTH consumers' default external-tier activation) with corpus-2 (4 skills from submodules/helix_agent/skills/postgres-mcp/*/SKILL.md), a domain-unrelated set that per pkg/skills/activate.go's CorpusTwoPolicy is TrustVendored and NEVER added to a default allowlist -- it is never actually co-activated with corpus-1 in any real deployment. Mixing it into the known_confusable/known_distinct derivation pulled the calibrated threshold down to an artificial 0.0256 that then refused the REAL corpus-1 tier on the project's own governance corpus (F-17). This corpus now separates the two: 'default_activation_eligible' entries are corpus-1 (the 8 constitution/skills/*/SKILL.md skills, all now carrying real YAML front-matter after F-16's frontmatter fix, PLUS speckit-analyze -- the 9th skill genuinely present in helix_code's .claude/skills/ external tier via the skill-activation pool symlink, so helix_code's real default-activated set is these 9; helix_agent's real default-activated set, over constitution/skills/ directly, is the same 8 minus speckit-analyze). The 4 postgres-mcp entries remain in this corpus for documentation/completeness (they are real skills an operator COULD explicitly allowlist alongside corpus-1) but are EXCLUDED from the known_confusable/known_distinct derivation in similarity.py -- see that file's CONFUSABLE/DISTINCT comments for the corpus-2-exclusion rationale.

skills.description: Use when a prompt begins with an UPPERCASE action token (BACKGROUND / REMINDER / ISSUE / BUG / TASK / a sub-system name) in any of the six §11.4.140 forms — `NAME :: rest`, `PREFIX::NAME :: rest`, `/NAME rest`, `/PREFIX::NAME rest`, `NAME ---> rest`, or the single-colon `NAME: rest` — or when the operator asks how the action-directive / slash-command system works, how to add a new directive, why a bare `/name` did not resolve, why an unregistered `TODO:` line correctly did nothing, or what a grammar-shaped token that is NOT registered should do. Also use before inventing ANY expansion for an unknown UPPERCASE token.
skills.name: Action Prefix System

skills.description: Validates media files (MP4, PNG, TXT) by running OCR, metadata checks, and pattern matching against expected content, returning PASS/FAIL with captured evidence. Use when a task needs to verify a recording, screenshot, or text-evidence file actually contains an expected pattern before a PASS is claimed — the §11.4.107/§11.4.163 anti-bluff media-validation oracle.
skills.name: media-validator
skills.note: HXC-159 F-17: real front-matter added (was previously body_derived=true, no front-matter at all -- F-01/F-16 fixed).

skills.description: Automatic multi-track ruler orchestration per §11.4.187 — one conductor session spawning, driving, resuming, monitoring and controlling per-track headless workers with per-subscription auth, rate-limit rebind and crash-resilient supervision. skills.description: Use whenever anything trackable is reported or discovered — a bug, a defect, a regression, a feature request, an internal task, a gap, "this is broken", "we should add X", "remember to do Y" — or when the operator invokes /issue, /bug, /task (or their /helix: and /default- forms, or the ISSUE/BUG/TASK action prefixes). Use it BEFORE answering a report in prose, and use it to check whether a report you are about to acknowledge has actually been turned into a real tracked item.

skills.description: Teaches an agent to record background/deferred work via the scheduled-work MCP server and — before ever reporting it done — to verify uncertain, blocked, or overdue items against real captured evidence. Use when dispatching background work, when a REMINDER fires and unconfirmed work must be re-checked, or before an autonomous loop declares its queue empty.
skills.name: scheduled-work-queue
